question:
A 23-year-old female college student visits her primary care physician reporting lifelong bone and
muscle aches that have recently intensified. She maintains an active lifestyle with a balanced diet and
has one sexual partner. The patient reports increased stress from final exams and occasional diarrhea.
Her current treatment with acyclovir for HSV shows minimal improvement. Physical examination
reveals 4/5 strength in all extremities and non-specific diffuse limb tenderness. Laboratory results
show: Serum: - Na+: 144 mEq/L - Cl-: 102 mEq/L - K+: 4.7 mEq/L - HCO3-: 24 mEq/L - Ca2+: 5.0 -
Urea nitrogen: 15 mg/dL - Glucose: 81 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL - Alkaline phosphatase: 225 U/L -
AST (GOT): 11 U/L - ALT (GPT): 15 U/L Which condition is most likely to be associated with this
clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Hyperphosphatemia from excessive dietary intake of
phosphate (B) Vitamin D deficiency due to limited sun exposure (C) Malabsorption due to celiac
disease (D) A genetic mutation affecting calcium-sensing receptors (E) Hypoalbuminemia leading to
pseudohypocalcemia (F) Anaphylaxis when receiving a transfusion (G) Sleep deprivation (H) Chronic
kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism (I) Rash over the metacarpophalangeal joints (J) A
history of anxiety/depression
 A. Sleep deprivation
B. Rash over the metacarpophalangeal joints
C. A history of anxiety/depression
D. Chronic kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism
E. Malabsorption due to celiac disease
F. Vitamin D deficiency due to limited sun exposure
G. Hyperphosphatemia from excessive dietary intake of phosphate
H. Anaphylaxis when receiving a transfusion
I. Hypoalbuminemia leading to pseudohypocalcemia
J. A genetic mutation affecting calcium-sensing receptors
